why: MI-280. Answers BL-20260909-A-BASE-BRANCH-RED-CAN-EXPIRE-THE-MANAGER-LEASE-OF-A-SESSION-THAT-IS-ALIVE-AND-HEARTBEATING. Tier-1: scripts/ops/manager_lease.py plus one test. No src/, no config/, no deploy/, no workflow, no order path. THE DEFECT, MEASURED 2026-09-09T08:05:10Z: status read heartbeat_at=07:34:57Z against a 90-minute TTL while the holder had heartbeated THREE more times, every one trapped in a PR that could not merge because an unrelated guard was red ON CLEAN MAIN. A cold session would have found that lease claimable. The lease lives in the repo so it survives its holder's DEATH -- correct -- but that makes its refresh a MERGE, and a merge is gated on green, so lease liveness depends on CI health, an unrelated property. THIS IS THE ROW'S OPTION (b) AND NOT (a)/(c), stated in the PR rather than implied: a heartbeat still cannot reach main while main is red. What changes is that the TTL is suspended and THE REASON IS RECORDED, so the register says 'could not refresh' rather than silently reading 'expired'. IT IS NOT A TTL WIDENING AND NOT A GUARD BYPASS, both ruled out by that row BY NAME: TTL_MINUTES is unchanged at 90, pinned by both a test and a self-test assertion, and no guard is skipped. THREE STATES PAST THE TTL, never collapsed: expired (main GREEN -- a heartbeat COULD have landed and did not) / unrefreshable (main RED -- NOT claimable) / expired_unverified (main UNKNOWN -- CLAIMABLE deliberately, because failing closed would make the lease unclaimable exactly when a manager has DIED and CI is unreachable, which is the case takeover exists for). THE READER IS ON BY DEFAULT -- a default-off flag would leave the collapse live for anyone who does not know to pass it -- and --no-check-main grades unknown, which is CLAIMABLE, so opting out can only ever be more permissive and can never block a takeover. ZERO CHECK RUNS IS `unknown`, NOT GREEN, which is the same trap CLAUDE.md documents for PRs and was VERIFIED LIVE (main's head really reported n=0 on 2026-09-12, cross-checked against the API), so it is the common case rather than a corner. 10 planted defects, 10 caught, positive control quiet. THE SCRIPT'S OWN SELF-TEST CAUGHT THIS CHANGE and is UPDATED RATHER THAN LOOSENED: the past-TTL cases now state their basis explicitly, because `expired` means 'could have refreshed and did not' and that is only knowable with one -- before the split they returned expired on no basis at all, which is the defect. handoff_check.py needed no change and that was VERIFIED BY RUNNING IT, not by reading it.
